mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes Citan petrol engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt M200 engine for the Citan 112 Petrol costs £1,600-£2,800 supply-only; a rebuilt M282 engine for the Citan 113 Petrol costs £2,300-£4,100 supply-only. Supply-and-fit adds £300-£600 labour.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure on a Mercedes Citan petrol engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rattling noise on cold start lasting more than 1-2 seconds is the classic warning sign on both M200 and M282 engines. The timing chain tensioner can lose hydraulic pressure, allowing chain slack and guide wear. Mercedes issued Workshop Bulletin WI-2021-045 for M282 tensioner issues.

mainEntity.name: What causes coil pack failure on a Mercedes Citan 112 Petrol?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M200 1.2-litre turbo petrol engine (based on the Renault Energy TCe 115) can suffer from coil pack failure, causing misfires and rough running. This is a common issue on higher-mileage units.

mainEntity.name: Is the Mercedes Citan petrol engine reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M200 and M282 petrol engines are generally reliable when properly maintained, but both have well-documented weaknesses. The M200 suffers from coil pack failure and timing chain tensioner wear, while the M282 is prone to timing chain tensioner issues (WI-2021-045) and cam phaser rattle. With these addressed, both engines are capable of 100,000+ miles.

mainEntity.name: How long do Mercedes Citan petrol engines last?

acceptedAnswer.text: Properly maintained M200 engines routinely reach 100,000-150,000 miles before major work. The M282 is too new for definitive long-term data but is showing good durability with regular servicing.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in my Mercedes Citan petrol?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if the Citan is otherwise in good condition with no structural rust or major transmission faults. A rebuilt M200 costs £1,600-£2,800 - far less than replacing a £4,000-£10,000 vehicle. The M282's higher value (£12,000-£25,000) makes replacement even more financially justifiable.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes Citan Petrol - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: Petrol Citans are significantly rarer than diesel in the UK, limited to the 1.2-litre M200 in the first-generation W415 and the 1.3-litre M282 in the second-generation W420. The M200, based on the Renault Energy TCe 115 engine, powered the 112 Petrol variant from 2013 to 2021 with 114hp. The M282, co-developed with the Renault-Nissan-Mitsubishi Alliance, arrived with the W420 generation in 2021, powering the 113 Petrol with 131hp. Both engines are turbocharged, direct-injection units, with the M282 featuring a gasoline particulate filter (GPF) to meet Euro 6d emissions standards.

milestones.description: M200.711, 1.2L turbo petrol, 114hp @ 4,500rpm, 190Nm torque (112 Petrol, W415 introduction)
M282 DE 14 AL, 1.3L turbo petrol, 131hp (113 Petrol, W420 launch)
M282 continues with minor refinement updates

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Mercedes Citan 112 Petrol and 113 Petrol is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points - from M200 coil pack failure to M282 timing chain tensioner wear and cam phaser rattle.
